newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica JSE says news feed to curb insider trading.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica JSE says news feed to curb insider trading.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's (JSE) new corporate electronic news service, to be launched on August 18, will reduce opportunities for insider trading, JSE listings director Mark Durr said on Thursday.
He said that the Stock Exchange News Service (SENS), through its equal, early and wide dissemination of price-sensitive data, will cut back the spread of privileged information on companies.
"SENS will reduce the window on insider dealing," Durr told reporters.

"No price-sensitive information will be allowed to be released to any third party during trading hours until it has been published by SENS," he said, adding that adherence to this would become a JSE listings requirement.

South Africa is burdened with the reputation of a being hot-bed of insider trading. The country has never successfully prosecuted anyone for the crime and financial authorities are currently drawing up new regulations in an attempt to curb it.

SENS will be transmitted by the major financial news agencies, giving equal access to all users of wire services. A "neutral" warning will be posted on the JSE's trading system five minutes before the release of any data to alert traders.
"The real purpose behind SENS is to enhance investor confidence," Durr said.

The JSE on Wednesday also released guidelines for companies on the dissemination of price-sensitive information. In it, it urged firms not to release such data to third parties or to allow it to filter into the market.

SENS, which will transmit information daily from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. (0600 to 1600 GMT), will have a two-month phasing-in period during which companies will not be obliged to use it. The requirement to release announcements through SENS will become obligatory from October 15.
In launching SENS, the JSE follows the example of other bourses worldwide, including the London Stock Exchange.
JSE president Russell Loubser said that through SENS and the company guidelines, the bourse hoped to play a role in curbing insider dealings.
"Hopefully we will very soon have some insider trading regulations with teeth. The JSE hopes to play a role in this," Loubser said.
